newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS crude edges up, prods slip on APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS crude edges up, prods slip on APIs.

text.p: U.S. oil products futures prices edged moderately lower while crude firmed a smidgen in after-hours ACCESS trade on Tuesday following mixed API weekly inventory data, players said.
The overnight market saw NYMEX February crude briefly jump 20 cents a barrel to $26.43 after the API reported a 9.5 million barrel draw on primary stocks for the week ending Jan.3.
But crude crept back down to only slightly above the NYMEX settlement price of $26.23, with some traders speculating values were largely offset by bearish refined products data.
U.S. heating oil and gasoline prices slipped about 0.40 cent a gallon in ACCESS action early Tuesday evening following the API estimates of significant builds during the prior week, players said.

The API data showed distillate stocks swelling by 2.9 million barrels and total U.S. gasoline stocks jumping by 4.3 million barrels, although daily gasoline production slipped by 150,000 barrels to 7.7 million.
East Coast gasoline stocks rose by 3.3 million barrels, including a 2.8 million gain in reformulated grades, the API said.
